theory.intro: **Power** is the rate at which an appliance uses electricity, measured in watts (W), where $1000\text{ W} = 1\text{ kW}$. **Energy** used is measured in kilowatt hours, and $\text{kWh} = \text{kW} \times \text{hours}$.
facts: Divide watts by $1000$ to get kilowatts, so a $2400$ W heater is a $2.4$ kW heater.
Multiply kilowatts by $1000$ to get back to watts, so $0.75$ kW is $750$ W.
Divide minutes by $60$ to get hours before multiplying, so $45$ minutes is $0.75$ h.
Energy in kilowatt hours is $\text{kWh} = \text{kW} \times \text{h}$, so the power must be in kW and not in watts.
Running cost is $\text{cost} = \text{kWh} \times \text{price per kWh}$, with a price in cents divided by $100$ first.
steps: Multiply kilowatts by hours to find energy, or divide energy by kilowatts to find hours
Multiply energy by the price per kWh to find cost, or divide cost by that price to find energy

workedExamples.question_text: Convert (a) $1850$ W to kilowatts and (b) $0.64$ kW to watts.

An appliance rated at $1600$ W runs for $45$ minutes. Electricity costs $27$ cents per kWh.
(a) Find the energy used in kWh.
(b) Find the running cost, to the nearest cent.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Power $=1600\div1000=1.6$ kW and time $=45\div60=0.75$ h.
Energy $=1.6\times0.75=1.2$ kWh.
(b) Price $=\$0.27$ per kWh.
Cost $=1.2\times0.27=\$0.324\approx\$0.32$.

workedExamples.question_text: A $1.8$ kW washing machine runs for $50$ minutes, three times each week. Electricity costs $30$ cents per kWh. Find its weekly running cost.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Total time $=3\times\frac{50}{60}=2.5$ h per week.
Energy $=1.8\times2.5=4.5$ kWh.
Weekly cost $=4.5\times0.30=\$1.35$.

workedExamples.question_text: A shop has $16$ lights, each rated at $35$ W. They run for $4.5$ hours a day on five days. Find their total energy use in kWh.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Total power $=16\times35=560$ W $=0.56$ kW.
Total time $=4.5\times5=22.5$ h.
Energy $=0.56\times22.5=12.6$ kWh.

workedExamples.question_text: A pump rated at $1400$ W costs $\$17.64$ to run. Electricity costs $28$ cents per kWh. How many hours did it run?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Energy $=17.64\div0.28=63$ kWh.
Power $=1400\div1000=1.4$ kW.
Time $=63\div1.4=45$ hours. Divide the cost by the price to find energy, then divide energy by power.

workedExamples.question_text:
Fridge A uses $540$ kWh a year. Fridge B uses $360$ kWh a year and costs $\$288$ more to buy. Electricity costs $32$ cents per kWh.
(a) Find the annual running-cost saving with B.
(b) How many years of these savings cover its extra purchase cost?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Energy saving $=540-360=180$ kWh a year.
Cost saving $=180\times0.32=\$57.60$ a year.
(b) $288\div57.60=5$ years. Compare the running-cost saving with the extra purchase cost.

workedExamples.question_text: A microwave rated at $1200$ W is used at $60\%$ power for $25$ minutes each day over $40$ days. Electricity costs $35$ cents per kWh. Find its running cost.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Power used $=1.2\times0.60=0.72$ kW.
Daily time $=\frac{25}{60}=\frac5{12}$ h.
Daily energy $=0.72\times\frac5{12}=0.3$ kWh.
Total energy $=0.3\times40=12$ kWh.
Cost $=12\times0.35=\$4.20$.

development.question_text:
A $3.6$ kW clothes dryer is run for $50$ minutes.
Electricity is charged at $28$ cents per kWh.
What does this cost?

A $1200$ W dishwasher runs for $1$ hour $30$ minutes, four times a week.
Electricity costs $34$ cents per kWh.
What is the cost of running it for one week, to the nearest cent?
development.solution_text:
$1200\text{ W} = 1.2\text{ kW}$
$\text{energy per run} = 1.2 \times 1.5$
$= 1.8\text{ kWh}$
$\text{energy per week} = 1.8 \times 4$
$= 7.2\text{ kWh}$
$\text{cost} = 7.2 \times \$0.34$
$= \$2.448$
$\approx \$2.45$

development.question_text:
A $2000$ W air conditioner runs for $5$ hours a day for $30$ days.
Electricity costs $\$0.29$ per kWh.
What is the total cost?
development.solution_text:
$2000\text{ W} = 2\text{ kW}$
$\text{energy per day} = 2 \times 5$
$= 10\text{ kWh}$
$\text{energy for }30\text{ days} = 10 \times 30$
$= 300\text{ kWh}$
$\text{cost} = 300 \times \$0.29$
$= \$87$

development.question_text:
An office runs $8$ desktop computers, each rated at $150$ W, for $9$ hours a day.
How much energy do they use in one day, in kilowatt hours?

A warehouse has $24$ lights, each rated at $45$ W, switched on for $11$ hours a day.
How much energy do they use in a $7$-day week, in kilowatt hours?
development.solution_text:
$\text{total power} = 24 \times 45$
$= 1080\text{ W}$
$= 1.08\text{ kW}$
$\text{energy per day} = 1.08 \times 11$
$= 11.88\text{ kWh}$
$\text{energy per week} = 11.88 \times 7$
$= 83.16\text{ kWh}$

development.question_text:
Running a $1.6$ kW pool pump cost $\$27.90$ when electricity was charged at $\$0.25$ per kWh.
For how many hours was the pump running?

A $900$ W games console used $21.6$ kWh of energy over one month.
For how many hours was it switched on?

Heater Model A is rated at $2400$ W and Model B at $2000$ W. Each is run for $6$ hours a day for $90$ days, with electricity at $\$0.30$ per kWh.
How much more does Model A cost to run?
development.solution_text:
$\text{difference in power} = 2400 - 2000$
$= 400\text{ W}$
$= 0.4\text{ kW}$
$\text{hours} = 6 \times 90$
$= 540\text{ h}$
$\text{extra energy} = 0.4 \times 540$
$= 216\text{ kWh}$
$\text{extra cost} = 216 \times \$0.30$
$= \$64.80$

mastery.question_text:
Every day a $900$ W microwave oven is used for $20$ minutes at $50\%$ power.
Electricity is charged at $\$0.32$ per kWh.
What is the cost of running the microwave for $365$ days?
mastery.solution_text:
$900\text{ W} = 0.9\text{ kW}$
$\text{power used} = 0.9 \times 0.5$
$= 0.45\text{ kW}$
$20\text{ min} = \dfrac{20}{60}\text{ h}$
$\text{energy per day} = 0.45 \times \dfrac{20}{60}$
$= 0.15\text{ kWh}$
$\text{energy for }365\text{ days} = 0.15 \times 365$
$= 54.75\text{ kWh}$
$\text{cost} = 54.75 \times \$0.32$
$= \$17.52$

mastery.question_text:
A standard refrigerator uses $620$ kWh per year.
An energy-efficient model costs $\$470$ more to buy and uses $385$ kWh per year.
Electricity costs $\$0.40$ per kWh.
After how many years does the saving on electricity cover the extra purchase price?
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{energy saved each year} = 620 - 385$
$= 235\text{ kWh}$
$\text{saving each year} = 235 \times \$0.40$
$= \$94$
$\text{time} = \dfrac{470}{94}$
$= 5\text{ years}$

mastery.question_text:
A $2500$ W vacuum cleaner uses $338$ kWh of energy over a year of $52$ weeks.
On average, how many hours and minutes is it used each week?
mastery.solution_text:
$2500\text{ W} = 2.5\text{ kW}$
$\text{energy per week} = \dfrac{338}{52}$
$= 6.5\text{ kWh}$
$\text{time} = \dfrac{6.5}{2.5}$
$= 2.6\text{ h}$
$0.6\text{ h} = 0.6 \times 60$
$= 36\text{ min}$
The vacuum cleaner is used for $2$ hours and $36$ minutes each week.
